text:
alex: ran a short nsys pass on the 1k-concurrent requests workload, dropping the trace here. main concern: top time is this unknown 'kv_prefetch_copy' and a big cudaMemcpyAsync spike right before fused_attn_forward. looks like prefetch might be hurting more than helping? tl;dr: need help ranking suspects and next checks.

alex: nsys summary (top time, ordered):
```
1) kv_prefetch_copy (23.4%)
2) fused_attention_forward (18.9%)
3) cudaMemcpyAsync (host->device) (14.7%)
4) softmax_kernel (9.2%)
5) elementwise_add (5.3%)
others... 28.5%
```

alex: timeline snippet: lots of small kv_prefetch_copy kernels interleaved with memcpy batches, then big fused_attention. SM% during fused_attn looks OK but overall SM util low (~40%).

maria: can you paste the exact nvtx spans? are we doing per-layer prefetch or global?

alex: NVTX is per-chunk: `prefetch:layer_{i}` before each KV load. code is basically: `cudaMemcpyAsync(dst_kv_buf+offset, src, size, stream_prefetch); kernel kv_prefetch_copy<<<...>>>` then later fused_attention uses that buffer.

tj: first thought: memcpy+small kernels -> PCIe stalls. If memcpys are synchronous on same stream as compute, they can serialize. Are you using separate streams?

alex: prefetch uses a dedicated stream `s_prefetch`. fused_attn runs on `s_main`. we used events to sync.

jin: saw similar pattern before — lots of tiny host->device copies create DMA thrash and reduce effective concurrency. two quick checks: coalesce prefetch ranges, or try cudaMemcpyAsync with pinned pooled buffers. also check if the copies are hitting UNIFIED or staging.

sam: agree with jin. also check L2 read/write hit rate. low L2 + many small transfers -> lots of time in memcpy. run `nsys -o out --stats true` and check L2_read_hit_rate and dram_read_throughput.

perf-bot: automated check complete: L2 hit rate ~12%, DRAM BW sat ~68% peaks, avg SM efficiency 42%, issue_count=mem-bound. (link to artifacts: https://ci.redwood/prof/1893456789) :robot_face:

maria: kernel shapes? if kv_prefetch_copy is launching many blocks with tiny workloads per block that's overhead. paste the `--kernel-summary` lines.

alex: kernel summary: `kv_prefetch_copy grid=(512,1,1) block=(128,1,1) time=23.4ms`, average per-call time 0.6ms, called 40 times. fused_attention grid=(1024,1,1) block=(256,1,1) time=18.9ms called 10 times.

tj: lots of kernel launch overhead. options: bump block size, fuse small copies into fewer larger copies, or use a single copy + offset pointer math in kernel.

jin: also try making kv_prefetch_copy use async memcpy for large contiguous ranges instead of device kernel memcopy — we saw device-side memcpy is slower for >64KB sometimes. but you said it's already cudaMemcpyAsync then a copy kernel — double work?

alex: we do memcpy async to prealloc device buffer then run a small kernel to do an unpack/deinterleave. maybe that kernel is unnecessary if we change data layout on host or do unpack on GPU in a fused op.

sam: to rank suspects: 1) small-copy/many-launch overhead (kv_prefetch_copy) 2) memcpy scheduling/PCIe contention 3) suboptimal block/grid sizing causing low SM occupancy 4) memory divergence inside fused_attention causing low IPC.

maria: next profiling steps I recommend (short):
- run `nv-nsight-cu-cli --print-gpu-trace` to see GPU/CPU overlap details
- collect `nvprof --metrics l2_cache_global_hit_rate,dram_read_transactions` on a smaller input to get counters
- instrument per-layer NVTX and repeat short run to attribute prefetch cost per layer
- try one experimental run: coalesce 4 layers per prefetch and compare top2 kernels

alex: will run nv-nsight and nvprof on smaller model slice and try coalescing. timeline experiment: if we combine 4 prefetches -> expected fewer kv_prefetch_copy launches (~10 instead of 40) and larger memcpy sizes.

tj: small tip: enable `cudaMemPrefetchAsync` only if using UVA and same memory pools — otherwise it can be a no-op and introduce overhead.

jin: also run `nvtxRangePush` around the host copy + cudaMemcpyAsync to ensure timeline shows copy start on host side. helps confirm ordering.

alex: planned experiments: (1) coalesce prefetch to 4-layer batches (2) replace device unpack kernel with host-side layout change + single memcpy (3) run nsight trace + nvprof counters. I'll post new trace.

sam: if that reduces kv_prefetch_copy from 23% -> <10% and memcpy drops, we win. if fused_attention time stays same but SM util improves, then check register pressure/occupancy with `cuobjdump --dump-sass` or `nsys` occupancy report.

maria: also add a canary with quantized kernels (int8) to see if memory-bound behavior shifts — sometimes quant reduces bandwidth pressure.

alex: thanks all. I'll run experiments and upload results in this thread. :thumbsup:
